summary.headline: Credo Brands Q2 FY27 revenue rose 16% YoY to INR189 crores, a record quarter, with EBITDA margin at 31.4% and PAT up 45%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue at INR189 crores (up 16% YoY), supported by positive same-store sales growth and better price realisations. Gross margin expanded 150 bps to 58.6% on richer product mix, and EBITDA grew 24% to INR60 crores at a 31.4% margin. H1 FY27 revenue grew 11% to INR314.6 crores, but H1 EBITDA margin slipped to 27.4% from 27.9% as advertising and brand-building spend rose to 6.7% of revenue. Management guided to 8-10% revenue growth and 8-10% marketing spend for the full year, while flagging geopolitical and inflationary caution.

financial_highlights.change: +16% YoY vs INR164 crores in Q2 FY26

segments.name: Channel mix Q2 FY27
segments.commentary: EBOs 47%, MBOs 36%, online 12%, LFS about 4%, others 1% of revenue.

segments.name: Channel mix H1 FY27
segments.commentary: EBOs 53%, MBOs 29%, online 12%, LFS 4%, others about 2% of revenue. Management said MBO growth may not be sustained at the Q2 pace, targeting about 10% growth.

segments.name: Mufti 2.0 format
segments.commentary: 14 stores opened in Q2 under the new identity (12 of them renovations), taking the total to 57 Mufti 2.0 stores. EBO count was 419 across 227 cities as of 30 Sep 2026.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 revenue growth guided at 8-10%, with management saying it should be achievable despite caution on geopolitics and inflation.
Full-year advertising and brand-building spend guided at 8-10% of revenue; management said actual could be 7% or 8.5%, and spend will be higher in subsequent quarters.
Next-year revenue growth and margins described as 'similar' to the current year guidance.
Brand investment expected to take at least a couple of years before it shows in bottom-line recovery; management says profitability could be impacted in the midterm.
Store renovations planned at about 20-30 in the current year, done during lean periods (Shradh in September and March).
capex_capacity: 57 stores now under the Mufti 2.0 identity, following 57 stores in roughly the last year; 14 added in Q2 FY27 including 12 renovations.
Expect about 20-30 further Mufti 2.0 store conversions in FY27; full conversion of the 400-plus EBO network will take a long time, constrained by remaining lease terms.
New-format stores reportedly grow about 8-10% after renovation.
Management says the company will reshape the network prioritising throughput per store over store count; expansion targets high-impact malls, high streets and airports.
Company remains debt-free with zero borrowings as of 30 Sep 2026.
demand_pricing: Same-store sales growth was positive for a third consecutive quarter. Management gave conflicting Q2 and H1 SSSG figures: H1 at 2.81% and Q2 at 3.0%, both corrected on the call.
Revenue per square foot was INR5,836 in H1 FY27 vs INR5,407 in H1 FY26.
Average selling prices rose across shirts, t-shirts and bottom wear in Q2; the gross margin gain was attributed to richer mix and better realisations.
Management said October trading was better than last year, though it did not quantify this.

Receivables were about INR285 crores at the end of September. Management attributed this to season-end stock transfers to distributors and said it normalises by March; it denied offering six-month credit.
Inventory was about INR130 crores on the books, including company-owned EBO and warehouse stock; management said it is monitored daily and weekly.

qa_highlights.question: Was there anything special in Q2 FY27, and can the momentum continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the business should be judged year-on-year, not quarter-on-quarter, and pointed to H1 revenue growth of about 11%. It guided 8-10% growth for the full year.

qa_highlights.question: Why are receivables (about INR285 crores) so high relative to H1 revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said receivables peak in September and March when new-season goods go to distributors and dues are not yet due; management said there have been no material bad-debt write-offs and that the position normalises by March.

qa_highlights.question: Do the marketing spend levels justify the returns (raised by an individual investor)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the spend a conscious multiyear investment, said recovery is not expected in the next one or two quarters, and said it would take at least a couple of years to show in bottom-line recovery. It cited no tangible return metrics beyond content testing.

qa_highlights.question: What are the like-for-like growth and the outlook for the full year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave H1 like-for-like growth of 2.81% and said full-year LFL could reach about 4-5%. It noted last year's Diwali timing made comparison unfair.

qa_highlights.question: Will marketing spend and revenue both rise in coming quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said marketing spend will be higher in subsequent quarters and that revenue will rise with it, with the 8-10% spend guide 'not cast in stone'.

qa_highlights.question: Will MBO growth continue, and what is the four-to-five-year vision?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the H1 MBO jump may not be repeated, with a target of about 10% growth. It declined to give four-to-five-year numerical guidance and said more clarity would come in the next year.

risks_watch: Brand investment is rising (6.7% of H1 revenue, 8-10% guided) while management says returns will take at least two years. H1 EBITDA margin already declined YoY.
Receivables of about INR285 crores at the reporting date; management's explanation of the seasonal pattern needs confirmation in Q3 and at March year-end.
Discretionary demand is exposed to geopolitical and inflationary pressure, which management flagged as a risk to consumer spending.
Uneven store execution: a retail investor reported non-renovated stores that were unclear on the Mufti 2.0 identity, and overheads for omnichannel staffing at low-volume stores were questioned.
Q2 SSSG was given inconsistently on the call (3.0% vs H1 2.81%), so reported figures should be verified against the investor presentation.
Management's ROE of 11.9% is still low despite zero debt; no target was given.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the operating turnaround and record Q2 numbers, but cautious on the outlook, citing geopolitics and inflation. Management was evasive on return on marketing spend and on long-term (4-5 year) targets, saying these will be clearer next year.
key_quotes: Our business is all about being able to sell everything we have produced profitably. As long as we can do that, we are on a good wicket.
So these are investments we are making. We don't look at them as expenses, and these would certainly impact profitability in the midterm.
Revenue also. We guided for 8% to 10% increase in revenue over last year, Nilesh, annually, and we have done 11% in H1.

adds.what: 14 Mufti 2.0 store format rollouts in Q2 FY27 (12 were renovations), taking total to 57 Mufti 2.0 stores
About 20-30 further Mufti 2.0 store conversions/renovations planned in FY27

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at 8-10% (midpoint 9%, held) and FY28 described as similar; Q2 revenue +16% with positive same-store sales and better realisations supports it, but no hard capacity or order numbers back the guide beyond a modest Mufti 2.0 store-renovation program of 20-30 stores, and management flagged geopolitical and inflation caution.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: H1 FY27 EBITDA margin fell to 27.4% from 27.9% as marketing rose to 6.7% of H1 revenue, guided to 8-10% for FY27, and management said profitability could be impacted in the midterm with bottom-line recovery taking at least a couple of years.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plants or factories discussed; only about 20-30 Mufti 2.0 store conversions planned in FY27 on a base of 419 EBOs, with 14 added in Q2 (12 renovations), so capacity growth is store-led and modest.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at 8-10% (held), H1 revenue up 11% to INR314.6 crores, and H1 like-for-like growth of 2.81% with full-year LFL possibly 4-5%; October trading reported better than last year but not quantified.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Company is debt-free with zero borrowings and capex discussion is limited to store renovations (20-30 in FY27); no plant utilisation or new capex announcement was flagged.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held FY27 guidance at 8-10% revenue growth and 8-10% marketing spend, flagged geopolitical and inflation caution, and said the 8-10% spend guide is 'not cast in stone' with spend rising in later quarters.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Marketing spend is set to rise above H1's 6.7% of revenue, and management flagged geopolitical and inflationary pressure on discretionary demand, so margin or revenue guidance could be trimmed.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Product launches were not discussed; the only new format is the Mufti 2.0 store identity, which is a store rollout rather than a product launch.

rows.label: Receivables of about INR285 crores to normalise by March
rows.why: Receivables stood at about INR285 crores at end-September, which management attributes to season-end distributor transfers and says normalises by March; this is not yet confirmed and the Q3 and March figures will test it.

rows.label: Brand investment payback over a couple of years
rows.why: Management said recovery is not expected in the next one or two quarters and bottom-line recovery needs at least a couple of years, with H1 EBITDA margin already down to 27.4% from 27.9%.

rows.label: MBO growth normalising to about 10%
rows.why: MBO channel was 36% of Q2 revenue and 29% of H1, but management said the H1 jump may not be sustained and targets about 10% growth.

tone.note: Management was confident on the record Q2 revenue and operating turnaround and held FY27 guidance, but cautious on margins and was evasive on marketing returns and 4-5 year targets, while analysts pressed on receivables, marketing payback and LFL growth.
